messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer prisma-ai reporting repeated timeouts on /v1/rerank during a traffic burst. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s and we see 502/504 + gateway timeouts. Window: 2026-03-16 11:07–11:15 UTC. QPS peaked ~950.

maya: Do you have the dashboard link and any example request_id or logs?

alex: Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/rerank?range=11:00-11:20
Sample runner log: ```[2026-03-16T11:09:12Z] request_id=abc123 runner=runner-7 status=502 error=timeout kvcache_misses=0 retries=3```

jordan: That looks like retry amplification. Clients retried, plus our gateway retry, plus runner queueing. Are client retries enabled for rerank? What are CB (circuit-breaker) metrics for runner-7?

luis: Circuit-breaker metrics: runner-7 cb_trips=4 in 10m, conn_count spike at 11:08, active_handles high. Also seeing a KV cache cold-start effect — many prefix misses at the same time.

alex: Repro I ran locally: ```ab -n 5000 -c 300 -p payload.json -T application/json http://api.redwood/v1/rerank``` Payload shape (trimmed): ```{"query":"best restaurants","candidates":["A","B",... (120 items)]}``` Observed ~15% requests timeout/502.

maya: How big are the candidates usually? 120 is large for rerank. Which model id?

alex: model: rerank-small-002, average candidates for this customer ~120, some bursts up to 200.

jordan: 120 candidates => ~120 forward-score ops per request. Under high concurrency that multiplies compute and memory per runner. If gateway sends many concurrent streams, KV cache thrash + GC pause and sockets backlog explains 5xx/timeouts.

luis: Immediate mitigations I propose: 
1) Instruct support to tell customer to reduce candidates per request (recommend <= 50).
2) Disable client-side immediate retries for rerank route (add jittered backoff doc).
3) Lower max_concurrency per runner from 64 -> 32 while we investigate.
4) Enable fallback routing to rerank-fast-001 (lighter model) for this customer until stable.
(note: increasing CB window hides problem, not fix it)

alex: I pushed a temporary routing policy for prisma-ai: max_concurrency=32 + fallback=rerank-fast-001. Watching now — error rate dropped from 12% -> 2% in last 5m.

maya: Please open an incident and attach runtime profiling/logs. Assign to eng-runtime. Also notify customer with repro and mitigation steps.

triage-bot: Incident created INC-20260316-789 by alex — severity: sev2, assignees: jordan,luis. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-789

jordan: Next steps for eng-runtime: collect flamegraphs and CPU/heap dumps for runner-7 in the 11:05–11:12 window, capture kernel tcp socket stats (netstat/snmp) and prefix cache hit/miss timeline. I'll own perf profiling.

luis: I'll add short-term per-route rate-limits and update the rerank runbook (KB) with guidance: max candidates per request, client-side backoff, and recommended model variants for high-throughput workloads. Also enable metrics to break down latency by candidate_count.

alex: Customer responded: "We see big improvement with fallback, thanks. We'll try reducing candidate lists and retesting." :thumbsup:

maya: :eyes: thanks team. After perf work, we should consider automatic candidate sharding or adaptive early-exit scoring to reduce worst-case cost for rerank under load.

jordan: Agreed — long-term: add adaptive batching + early-exit when top-k stabilized, and instrument per-candidate micro-timings. For now I'll collect profiles and upload to INC-20260316-789.

alex: Leaving notes in the incident: repro steps, ab command, sample log, temporary routing change, observed drop in errors. Closing the support ticket as "mitigated, investigating".

luis: Also will add a short blurb to the support KB about avoiding heavy candidate lists and how to use rerank-fast-001 as a cheaper fallback.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up once flamegraphs are in.
